entries.title: The guardian waits for your arrow
items: The guardian now stays put until your arrow has passed through, then slides to its new spot.
In How to play, clearing a lesson now shows your progress — the lessons you've done so far and the next one up.
Settings, the contact form and pop-up dialogs now share a cleaner, more consistent look.
Your coins now show the first time you open the game, not just after visiting Settings.
If you sign in and we don't have your birth year, we'll now ask for it.

entries.title: Guardian stones slide into place
items: Guardian stones now wait for your arrow to pass through, then slide to their new spot.
Finish a lesson in How to play and you'll see your progress through all 21 and a button to the next one.
Pop-up dialogs, the How to play bubble and the support form now match the refreshed Settings look, with tidier spacing.
When you sign in, you may be asked for your birth year to finish setting up your account—or just tap 'Not now'.

entries.title: Smoother menus and dialogs
items: Menus, pop-ups and expanding sections now open and close with smooth, consistent motion, and opening a quick answer no longer scrolls the page on its own.
Cloud save works again — if your progress had stopped syncing with a 'newer version' message, it now loads and saves to the cloud as before.
The Help and news screen is tidier: your support messages now sit on cards, each with its own title and chat-style bubbles, and the coin counter no longer overlaps the tabs.
On Android, the Back button now closes Settings, and closes any panel open on top of it first.
In Settings, your account card now shows your profile name — the same name on your profile and the boards — instead of the sign-in gamertag.

entries.title: Add friends by tapping players
items: Tap another player in the leaderboards, rooms or match history to open their card and send them a friend request.
You now get a username automatically (like 'SwiftArrow482'), so you show up on the leaderboards right away—and you can change it once to a name of your own.
Settings has a cleaner new look, organised into two tabs: 'Settings' and 'Help and news'.

entries.title: Skills now count on the leaderboard
items: Win with the prince's skills on and your score now counts on the leaderboard, at full points — the skills are earned by playing, so they no longer keep your win off the board.
Friend challenges now work with the prince's skills on: you can send one after such a win, and your friend plays it with their own skills and can win it with them on.

entries.title: Help and news in Settings
items: You can now report a problem or suggest an idea from Settings, follow the replies, and sign up for game news by email.
The game now downloads a lot less in your browser, so it starts faster.
New players now go straight into level 1, with a hand pointing to your first move, instead of signing in or reading a tutorial first.
Signing in works again on Android, so your leaderboards and settings sync.

entries.title: One save across your devices
items: The game now syncs your progress the moment it starts and keeps a single save, so switching between the web and your phone no longer asks you to choose a save.
When you play on more than one device, your progress is now combined correctly, so nothing you've earned gets lost or counted twice.

entries.title: First bump free after ward moves
items: After the ward moves, your first bump into it is free — no lost heart, and your combo keeps going
The game page is now just the game with no scrolling, and About has moved to a link in the bar

entries.title: Share your daily result anywhere
items: Share your daily result through your device's share menu — one Share button, pick Post or Story — and the board, hearts, flame and QR are back on the picture
When your avatar wears its rank frame, the white or dark background behind it is gone for a cleaner look
The play page footer now reads © 2026 VGraphics with Company, Terms and Privacy links, and Settings gains a Company link beside Privacy

entries.title: New star and chest sounds
items: When you clear a level, your stars now pop in with cheerful rising notes, the third lands with a magic sparkle, and a full three-star chest rattles with coins before bursting open.

entries.title: Rank frames on your picture
items: Each player's picture now has a frame that shows their rank — you'll see it on leaderboards, player cards, rooms, match history and more. Pick your own on your VHub profile.

entries.title: Story music fades in and out
items: In the storybook, the music now fades smoothly in and out instead of cutting off, and it fades gently each time it loops.
When you open the game, your profile picture and name are ready as you reach the map, instead of popping in a moment later.
Before you delete your account, the "Confirm it's you" step now rejects a different Google account with a clear message, so nothing happens by mistake.

entries.title: One curse clock on guardian levels
items: On guardian levels, one clock now counts the curse down: its bar empties and the numbers turn amber, then red, as time runs low, and you win time back with every hit.
Ice from spells and frost now keeps its number well apart from the ice already on the board, so you won't get two almost-identical ice blocks.
Lists and the level map now stop cleanly at their ends instead of scrolling past them.
If you pick the wrong Google account when confirming a data deletion, the message now names the right account to use instead of just saying it couldn't confirm it's you.

The privacy policy now explains that your account, name, picture, blocked players, settings and the global leaderboards are handled through VHub, and it covers Google profile photos and how to delete your data.

entries.title: Share your Daily as a picture
items: Share your finished Daily as a picture of your solved board, with every arrow bursting out — post it anywhere or send it straight to your story.
Your profile picture now shows in place of the preset avatars — to pick a preset instead, remove your picture.
The preset avatars now slide smoothly in and out of view.

entries.title: Your settings follow you everywhere
items: When you're signed in, your settings — Music, Sounds, Vibration, Tap twice to launch and Show story pages — follow you across your devices, and changes you make in your avatar menu on the site show up in the game right away.
The "Sign in with Google" button now appears in your language, and the sign-in window opens and closes more smoothly.
The About panel now notes that your settings travel with you.

entries.title: Your profile photo now shows
items: Your profile picture now shows across the game — on your account button, your profile, and in boards and rooms.
On your profile, your name now sits next to your picture, with a small note beneath it that it can't be changed.

entries.title: Stories play again
items: Fixed a glitch so stories play again in your browser — before, no story could load.

entries.title: Neater top row on wide windows
items: On a wide browser window, the top row of buttons and the coin counter now line up neatly with the buttons along the sides of the board, instead of floating over the map.

entries.title: Account button on the home screen
items: A new account button sits at the top right of the home screen — tap it to sign in, or, once you're signed in, see your picture and open your profile.

entries.title: Sharper story pictures on big screens
items: Story pictures now look sharp on big screens instead of pixelated
Boss shields that move now wait for your arrow, then drop neatly into place

entries.title: Clearer, fairer guardian fights
items: The guardian's health bar is now a slim strip that covers far less of the board, and the board no longer shifts when a status icon appears or disappears mid-fight.
In a guardian fight, a magic wand or Double-Shot's extra arrow now counts as a single move against rage, so it can strike you at most once and won't cost you extra hearts.
On a PC, the leaderboard, the win-screen ranking and your profile are now shown larger and easier to read.
On levels with more than one ice block or shutter, their countdown numbers are now spaced further apart instead of being nearly identical.
In your profile, choosing a preset avatar now keeps your picture, and a 'Remove picture' option appears wherever your picture shows, including on the web.
The 'How to play' guide now explains that touching a guardian's ward costs you a heart.

entries.title: No changes you'll notice
items: Improvements and fixes.

entries.title: New About section below the game
items: Scroll below the game for a new About section — how to play, what's inside, answers to common questions and handy links. The "About this game" button takes you straight there, then back to the game.
The page now shows a copyright line and a link to our Terms.

entries.title: On/off switches replace checkboxes
items: On/off options now use a switch that slides across and turns green when on, in place of the old tick boxes and On/Off labels.
In the browser, the page's text no longer gets selected and the right-click and long-press menus stay closed while you play; typing in text fields still works as normal.

entries.title: The Tangled Tower: a story and 17 guardians
items: A story in 81 painted pages: Prince Arlo and Pip the owl climb the Tower of Worlds to break the Duskweaver's curse. Read it from the new Story button on the map.
A guardian waits at the top of every world, from level 20: send arrows out of the top to free it before the curse clock runs out.
Earn up to three stars on every level, keep a daily streak and level up the prince's skills.

entries.title: The Tangled Tower: a story and 17 guardians
items: A story in 81 painted pages: Prince Arlo and Pip the owl climb the Tower of Worlds to break the Duskweaver's curse. Read it from the new Story button on the map.
A guardian waits at the top of every world, from level 20: send arrows out of the top to free it before the curse clock runs out.
Earn up to three stars on every level, keep a daily streak and level up the prince's skills.
A new start: the VGraphics intro, then Exitwise's own key art while the game loads, over a squishy new loading bar.
The level map is painted in a new style for all 17 worlds, and fills wide windows edge to edge.
The dots of the board's grid are easier to see.
Settings fits wide windows: two groups side by side, with nothing to scroll.
All 17 world backgrounds and all 12 animal avatars are redrawn with brand-new art.
Fresh icons for the powerups, the coin, the tutorial hand and the map editor's bomb tool.
New background music for the menu and the levels.
Eleven new sound effects, including bombs, clicks, losing a heart and completing a level.
Lighter audio files, for a smaller download.
Real sound effects across the whole game, in place of the old beeps.
Sign in with Google or Play Games and get a one-time thank-you of 100 coins for linking your account.
The level map opens on your current level, scrolls smoothly, and celebrates when a new world unlocks.
On landscape and other wide screens, everything is about 30% bigger and the board fills the window.
Your privacy choices now control ads and analytics.
Play with friends keeps a history of your last 50 matches, and you can share any match's results as a picture.
The host picks the world and the lives for a match, and each game scores points for speed, hearts left and your place.
Your profile photo now shows everywhere: in rooms, on the leaderboards, on profiles and on map cards.
Switches are now keys and their gates locked doors, and portals have coloured rims and numbers, so matching ends are easy to spot.
How to play lets you watch each move play out before you go on to the next lesson.
Exitwise is out, on Google Play and in your browser.
New How to play: short lessons that bring in each obstacle one at a time, with a hand that shows every tap.
Daily, Ranking, Friends and Maps are round buttons near the top of the home screen, leaving more room for the map.
In rooms everyone plays exactly the same board, from Easy to a much bigger Expert that uses every obstacle.
